sentences.text: Montsecosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorphs that belongs to the Neosuchia clade.
The skull of Montsecosuchus depereti was less than half the length of its presacral vertebrae.
This animal shares the trait of having three sacral vertebrae with the genus Alligatorellus.
A notably short radius is a unique characteristic of the genus Montsecosuchus.
The holotype specimen, MGB 512, is a nearly complete articulated skeleton housed in the Museu de Ciències Naturals de Barcelona.

The genus Montsecosuchus was described by Buscalioni and Sanz in 1990, with the type species originally named Alligatorium depereti by Vidal in 1915 from fossils found in the Montsec Lithographic Limestone quarry in Spain.

Montsecosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago during the Barremian stage, and fossils date to the Upper Berriasian to Lower Valanginian stages.
